title: Counting the Benefit Periods of the Year That Have Passed
content:
How many benefit periods of the year have passed on a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card, for the purpose of an allowance still owed, is counted on the basis the card's allowance is loaded on and on whether the card carries any entry at all.

**The rule.** The benefit periods that have passed are counted as the whole quarters of the benefit year gone by, where the card's allowance is loaded on calendar quarters of the benefit year and the card carries at least one entry; as a single period of which none has passed, where the card's allowance is made available once a year; and as the whole months of the benefit year gone by in every other case.

| The card | How the periods that have passed are counted |
|---|---|
| its allowance is loaded on calendar quarters of the benefit year, and its record carries at least one entry | the whole quarters of the benefit year gone by |
| its allowance is made available once a year | the benefit year counts as a single period, of which none has passed |
| any other case | the whole months of the benefit year gone by |

The whole quarters or months gone by are counted from the first day of the benefit year to the day the reckoning is made. An entry on the card is any entry at all on its running record, of whatever kind.

**A point of judgement.** The first row asks two things at once. A card loaded on calendar quarters whose record is still empty does not satisfy it, and the periods that have passed are then counted as the whole months of the benefit year gone by.

**Worked through on hypothetical dates.** Where 7 whole months of the benefit year have gone by: on a card loaded on calendar quarters carrying entries, 2 whole quarters have passed and the current period is the third of the year; on a card whose allowance is made available once a year, none has passed; on a card loaded on calendar months, 7 have passed.
